GC Update

General Contractor — Status Change

⚠ GC Transition — Don Burns / TWD Investments Now Leading

We came across Narrative Contracting, LLC through a referral from Bret Barnhart — we didn't have a prior relationship with them. Early on we had a concern that their approach was skewing toward commercial-grade construction methods when this project is really built more like a large house — wood-frame, residential in nature.

Their initial estimate was around $1.8M. When we pushed to understand why costs had climbed from there, they weren't willing to open up the details — which subs had come in high, what was driving specific line items, or whether there was room to push prices lower. Without that visibility we had no real ability to negotiate or validate what was inflating the number. We made the decision to move on.

Narrative did produce a conceptual budget of $1,941,638 which was prepared for financing and due diligence purposes (9/2/2025). That budget — including its $162,141 contingency and $145,927 GC fee — is the basis of our current financing package. We're using it as the baseline even though Narrative is no longer our contractor.

Don Burns of TWD Investments is our current GC. We're working through bids with him now in a much more open and collaborative fashion — full line-item visibility, subs sharing actual numbers, real back-and-forth on where costs can move. Our target remains $1.7M in construction costs. Mike's Texas benchmark ($1.4M hard costs + $200K GC fee = $1.6M all-in for a comparable 20-unit near CO) gives us strong data to work with in that process.

We will update this page when Don's bid is finalized and the construction contract is executed.

Comparable Benchmark — Why $1.7M Is Achievable

Mike's Texas Build — Similar Scope · 20 Units · Near CO
Mike (MCK partner) is building a comparable 20-unit project in Texas right now — 2–3 weeks from certificate of occupancy. His total hard construction spend is $1.4M plus $200K in GC fee paid to the contractor and partners. That's $1.6M all-in for a finished comparable project. The Narrative Contracting baseline bid at $1.94M includes contingency and GC fee. Don Burns / TWD Investments is now working bids against this baseline — our target of $1.7M is well-supported by Mike's numbers.

Lesson Learned — Permit Risk

We closed on this dirt January 15 and have been carrying it ever since — waiting weeks for structural engineering, then working through five permit resubmissions. The build itself is a 9-month project — the permit is the variable nobody warned us about.

The next time I write a contract on land to build something in the City of Tulsa, the closing date will be contingent on permit issuance — structured as "close within 2–3 weeks of receiving permit." That one clause eliminates carrying cost risk on dirt you're not building on yet and keeps your capital working. It's the thing I'd do differently from day one on this deal.

Update Log

Monthly updates

August 2025
Update #1 · Initial

Where we are: Land closed at $146,203. Architectural fees ($23,359), structural engineering ($11,000), and civil engineering — Wallace Design Collective ($35,530) — all paid in full. Permit submitted to City of Tulsa, currently in review (5th submission). $216,092 total cash deployed to date.

GC: Narrative Contracting, LLC (referred through Bret Barnhart) produced a conceptual bid of $1,941,638 for financing and due diligence purposes on 9/2/2025. After they were unwilling to open up sub-level detail and negotiate transparently, we made the decision to move on. Don Burns / TWD Investments is now our GC. Working through bids with him now with full line-item visibility. Narrative's budget remains the basis of our financing package. Target construction cost: $1.7M. Mike's Texas build ($1.4M hard + $200K GC fee = $1.6M all-in) is our benchmark.

Appraisal: Ace Appraisal Group completed a fee simple appraisal, valuing the completed project at $2,160,000 effective 10/1/2026. As-is land value: $220,000. Total project cost at current budget: $2,167,731. The math on the flip tightens significantly if we hit $1.7M on construction — that's the primary lever.

Permit: We closed on the land January 15, waited several weeks for the structural engineering report, then submitted for permit. We've been carrying this dirt since January. We've now resubmitted five times working through city comments. The permit is the active bottleneck. Expected build time once we break ground is 9 months to CO. Everything else — GC, financing, design — is ready. We're waiting on the city.

Lesson on the land purchase: Next time I write a contract on land to build in the City of Tulsa, closing will be contingent on permit — structured as "close within 2–3 weeks of receiving permit from the city." That keeps you from sitting on dirt and carrying land cost before you're building. It's the main thing I'd do differently on this deal.

Next update: September 2025 — permit status, Don Burns / TWD Investments bid finalized, updated construction number.
